handbookNote: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (DNR) boating safety program (dnr.wisconsin.gov/topic/Boat) -- Wisconsin has no single official state-administered boating knowledge exam; Wis. Stat. ch. 30 and DNR's own boater-education guidance (dnr.wisconsin.gov/Education/OutdoorSkills/safetyEducation) require operators born on or after January 1, 1989 to hold a Wisconsin boating safety certificate (or recognized out-of-state/NASBLA equivalent, or a Canadian Pleasure Craft Operator Card) to operate a motorboat or personal watercraft, which in practice means completing a DNR-approved NASBLA-aligned course whose own embedded final exam serves as the qualifying test rather than a separate DNR-run exam -- this mandate and its birth-date cutoff were independently confirmed by two sources: Wisconsin DNR's own safety-education page and Boat-Ed's official Wisconsin course page (boat-ed.com/wisconsin), both agreeing on the Jan. 1, 1989 cutoff and the PWC minimum operating age of 12 (with mandatory course completion and no supervision exception, versus a tiered supervised/certified structure for motorboats operated by 10-15 year-olds) -- exam-format convergence was independently confirmed across two approved vendors: Boat-Ed Wisconsin (unit quizzes >=70%, final exam >=80%, unlimited attempts, ~3-4 hours, $55.95) and iLearnToBoat Wisconsin (final exam >=80%, unlimited attempts, ~2-3 hours, $75.95 including the $1 DNR fee), converging on an 80% final-exam passing threshold with unlimited retakes; the exact final-exam question count is not consistently published by Wisconsin's approved vendors and is therefore left unconfirmed rather than asserted -- content is also grounded in real Wisconsin-specific detail independently verified against DNR's own published pages: the broad statutory vessel/registration definition and HIN/documented-vessel handling (dnr.wisconsin.gov/permits/registrations/boat), PFD/life-jacket requirements including the wearable-PFD-per-person and 16-foot-plus throwable-device rules, PWC-operator wear mandate, and the federal under-13 open-vessel PFD rule (dnr.wisconsin.gov/Topic/Boat/LifeJackets), and boating accident reporting thresholds and procedure -- $2,000 property-damage/death/injury-beyond-first-aid/total-loss trigger, immediate verbal report plus a 10-day written Form 4100-020 report, up to a $326 penalty for noncompliance, and Wis. Stat. 30.67(4)'s bar on using accident-report information as trial evidence (dnr.wisconsin.gov/Topic/Boat/CrashInfo) -- plus Wisconsin Administrative Code ch. NR 5 (Boat Rules and Registration), including its framework for lake-specific modification/waiver of slow-no-wake speed restrictions (NR 5.20-5.21) and registration-transfer requirements (NR 5.02); Wisconsin's general 0.08% BUI blood alcohol standard is presented as the uniform national baseline applied under Wis. Stat. ch. 30, since the exact BUI statute section and full penalty schedule were not independently re-verified against current statute text in this build (the same honest-hedge approach used for Missouri and Maryland boating in this project) -- plus universal NASBLA-aligned boating-safety fundamentals (Navigation Rules, U.S. Aids to Navigation System, required equipment, navigation lights and sound signals, cold-water immersion, weather, and towed water sports) applied to Wisconsin's extensive inland lake system, which drives the state's major recreational boating culture and its northern-climate cold-water risk profile emphasized in DNR's own spring safety messaging -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
